Giannis Antetokounmpo is a Greek and Nigerian professional basketball player for the Milwaukee Bucks of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Antetokounmpo's nickname is "Greek Freak".
Antetokounmpo led the Bucks in all five major statistical categories during the 2016–17 season.
Antetokounmpo received the Most Improved Player award in 2017.
Antetokounmpo has received eight All-Star selections.
Antetokounmpo won consecutive NBA Most Valuable Player Awards in 2019 and 2020.
Antetokounmpo was named the NBA Defensive Player of the Year in 2020.
Antetokounmpo led the Bucks to their first NBA championship since 1971 during the 2021 season.
Antetokounmpo was designated as the flag bearer for the Paris 2024 Olympic Games by the Greek Olympic Committee.
Antetokounmpo's official surname became Αντετοκούνμπο, the Greek transcription of Adetokunbo.
Giannis Antetokounmpo was born in Athens to Nigerian parents.
Antetokounmpo began playing basketball for the youth teams of Filathlitikos in Athens at a young age.
In 2011, Antetokounmpo began playing for the club's senior team before entering the 2013 NBA draft.
Antetokounmpo was selected 15th overall by the Bucks in the 2013 NBA draft.
Antetokounmpo made his NBA debut on October 13, 2013.

Antetokounmpo was named to the All-NBA Second Team after his breakout season with the Bucks.

Antetokounmpo recorded a then career-high 52 points in a loss to the Washington Wizards on December 23, 2016.
Antetokounmpo was named an Eastern Conference All-Star team starter for the 2017 NBA All-Star Game.
Antetokounmpou scored 41 points and made his first game-winning buzzer-beater in a win over the New York Knicks on January 6, 2017.
Antetokounmpo was named to the Eastern Conference Player of the Month for games played in March 2017.
Antetokounmpo led the Bucks in every one of the five major statistical categories (points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks) during the 2016–17 regular season.
Antetokounmpo was named NBA MVP in 2019.

Antetokounmpo was named NBA Finals MVP after leading the Bucks to their first championship since 1971.
Antetokounmpo scored a career-high and Bucks record 64 points against the Indiana Pacers on December 13, 2023.

Antetokounmpo helped Greece finish ninth overall in the 2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup with a 5–1 record.
Antetokounmpo was critical to the Bucks' early success during the 2018–19 season, earning the Eastern Conference Player of the Month awards for October, November, December and February.

Antetokounmpo is officially listed as a forward and sometimes described as a point forward, but has been deployed across all five positions.
Antetokounmpo established himself as one of the league's most devastating slashers and transition scorers by the 2016–17 season.
Antetokounmpo increased his jump-shooting output in the 2019–20 season, averaging a career-high 4.4 three-point goals attempted and 1.4 made per game.
Antetokounmpo has developed his own version of the Euro step, described by Jordan Brenner as "the final phase of the move's evolution".

Antetokounmpo is recognized as an elite defensive player capable of guarding all five positions but more often deployed in a "free safety" role that allows him to roam the paint and discourage attacks on the rim.
Antetokounmpo has become a perennial NBA All-Defensive honoree.
